newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week ending Aug 23.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week ending Aug 23.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday reported a 40 percent rise in its turnover in the week ending August 23, and traders said the activity was driven by higher market liquidity.
The value of the BSE's weekly turnover hit 44.064 million dinars ($8.95 million) in 169 transactions, rising 39.7 percent over the previous week's total of 31.535 million dinars.
Traders said the third week of the month is traditionally characterised by higher liquidity, with banks and companies having surpluses because there are no pay-outs of salaries and pensions.
The central bank short-term bonds again grabbed the lion's share in the BSE weekly turnover, taking 20.27 million dinars.
The National Bank of Yugoslavia on Friday auctioned a new tranche of its bonds, raising their interest rate to 102.88 percent from 60.7 percent. The bonds' life was shortened from 60 to 30 days.
The commercial paper segment saw 135 transactions worth 17.234 million dinars. The interest rates on those securities ranged from 44 to 971 percent a year and maturity ran from five to 90 days.

The most actively traded securities were those issued by chemicals producer Hipol (2.6 million dinars), food processor BIM Slavija (1.8 million dinars) and trading company Jugometal (1.8 million dinars).
The bourse reported two deals in forward wheat contracts worth 3.745 million dinars, with a kilo of wheat fetching 0.9 dinars.
